gen-fs-styro-gf-chocolate-classical-sans: Commanding and a bit retro, Styro packs its big lowercase letters so tightly the curves nearly close up, while Chocolate Classical Sans keeps its strokes open.
gen-fs-styro-gf-comme: Comme reads smooth and open, its curves never clogging up. Against Styro's crammed, retro heading, that looseness is what makes the pair work: one crowds its letters together, the other lets them breathe.
gen-fs-styro-gf-cossette-texte: Chunky, retro and unapologetic: Styro pinches its joints and flares its ends, while Cossette Texte has none of that fuss. Its wide-eyed e keeps a long stretch of text easy going.
gen-fs-styro-gf-duru-sans: Styro crams its big lowercase letters together until the openings nearly vanish, a retro, commanding look. Duru Sans sits beside it with wide openings on small letters, so the heading's tightness has somewhere to rest.
gen-fs-styro-gf-fresca: Retro and commanding, Styro closes its letters up tight with barely a gap in the e or c. And Fresca keeps its counters connected to the outside, with horizontals as thick as its verticals.
gen-fs-styro-gf-funnel-sans: Crowded, closed-up letters define Styro's retro swagger. Funnel Sans keeps its strokes the same width from stem to curve and opens its e wide, so a long block of text moves along smoothly.
gen-fs-styro-gf-gafata: Styro presses its retro, commanding lowercase together until the e and c nearly seal shut. Gafata has a tall band of letters under short stalks, and its wide-eyed e makes a long passage go down easily.
gen-fs-styro-gf-geist: Crowded, retro and loud, Styro packs its letters until the e and c barely open. Geist is the opposite: a quiet, level beat with openings wide as a sprung paper clip.
gen-fs-styro-gf-georama: Styro's tightly packed, nearly closed e and c give it a retro, commanding punch that fits big, short words. Georama stays approachable, with a wide-open c like a bracelet pulled apart.
gen-fs-styro-gf-gidole: Retro, crowded and bold, Styro huddles its letters. Gidole's terminals stay apart like open scissor blades, and its high midline and neon-tube strokes mean you can size it up or down freely.
